text: Scene 11 The Book
speaker: C2

text: Dorian sits and begins to read.
speaker: C2

text: It was the strangest book he had ever read.
speaker: C2-4

text: A poisonous book. The heavy odour of incense seemed to cling about its pages and to trouble the brain.
speaker: C5

text: Within its defiling pages a story
speaker: C4

text: A disordered account of a young Parisian trying to experience all the passions, depravities and perversions
speaker: C2

text: from every century
speaker: All

text: It seemed to Dorian that all the sins of the world were passing in dumb show before him.
speaker: C6

text: He read on oblivious to the pervading influences rising from the fetid pages
speaker: C4

text: To the noxious thoughts seeping into his mind.
speaker: C2

text: To the insidious evil penetrating his soul
speaker: C5

text: To the tendrils of desire coiling within his loins
speaker: C4

text: And unconscious of the creeping shadows that engulfed him
speaker: C2

text: He read on in the fading light as he devoured the book
speaker: C6

text: or perhaps the book devoured him.
speaker: All

text: His valet reminded him of the lateness of the hour and that he was to dine with Lord Henry.
speaker: C4

text: I am so sorry, Harry, but really it is entirely your fault. That book you sent me so fascinated me that I forgot the time.
speaker: Dorian

text: Yes, I thought you would like it.
speaker: Lord Henery

text: I didn't say I liked it, Harry. I said it fascinated me. There is a great difference.
speaker: Dorian

text: Ah, you have discovered that?
speaker: Lord Henery

text: For years, Dorian Gray could not free himself from the influence of this book.
speaker: C2

text: Or perhaps he never sought to free himself from it.
speaker: C4

text: The whole book seemed to him to contain the story of his own life, written before he had lived it
speaker: C4

text: He was more fortunate than the novel's fantastic hero. He never knew that grotesque dread of mirrors, polished metal surfaces, and still water which came upon the young Parisian.
speaker: C5

text: And so he lived by the book. A new Hedonism that was to save life from that harsh uncomely puritanism
speaker: C6

text: Its aim, indeed, was to be experience itself
speaker: C4

text: It was noticed, however, that some of those who had been most intimate with him appeared, after a time, to shun him.
speaker: C8

text: Women who had wildly adored him, and for his sake had braved all social censure were seen to grow pale with shame or horror if Dorian Gray entered the room.
speaker: C2

text: I hear he is a man whom no pure-minded girl should be allowed to know.
speaker: C8

text: And whom no chaste woman should sit in the same room with.
speaker: C4

text: I hear his friendship is fatal to young men.
speaker: C2

text: There was that wretched boy in the Guards who committed suicide.
speaker: C8

text: I heard that his friend, Sir Henry Ashton, had to leave England with a tarnished name.
speaker: C4

text: What about Adrian Singleton and his dreadful end?
speaker: C2

text: What about Lord Kent's only son and his career? I hear his father is broken with shame and sorrow.
speaker: C5

text: What about the young Duke of Perth? What sort of life has he got now? What gentleman would associate with him?
speaker: C4

text: And Lady Gwendolen, not a breath of scandal had ever touched her. There is not a single decent woman in London now who would drive with her in the park
speaker: C2

text: Lord Gloucester showed me a letter that his wife had written to him when she was dying alone in her villa. Dorian Gray was implicated in the most terrible confession I ever read.
speaker: C6

text: But the wonderful beauty that had so fascinated Basil Hallward, and many others besides him, seemed never to leave him.
speaker: C5

text: Even those who had heard the most evil things against him could not believe anything to his dishonour when they saw him.
speaker: C6

text: Over the years it was the portrait that gathered the evil.
speaker: C5

text: It became more twisted, more hideous with each vile deed.
speaker: C8

text: It held an awful fascination for Dorian Gray,
speaker: C5

text: For weeks he would forget the hideous painted thing hidden above him. Then, wherever he was the urge to be with it overtook him.
speaker: C6

text: He would sit in front of the picture, sometimes loathing it and himself.
speaker: C5

text: Other times smiling with secret pleasure at the misshapen shadow that had to bear the burden that should have been his own.
speaker: C8

text: And so he continued his hedonistic journey
speaker: All
